newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DORTMUND POLICE RELEASE MANCHESTER FANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND POLICE RELEASE MANCHESTER FANS.

text.p: German police said on Thursday they had released all Manchester United supporters detained surrounding the club's clash with Borussia Dortmund and hailed their bid to defuse tension between fans as a success.
Police temporarily detained some 200 people for minor public order offences connected with Wednesday's European Cup semifinal first leg. Around 120 were Germans.
The build-up to the game, which Dortmund won 1-0, had been the subject of concern as Manchester fans were involved in trouble at the club's last away tie in Portugal.
Eight English fans were injured after a clash with riot police following their quarter-final at Porto.
The Dortmund authorities' decision to hold a street party for the visiting fans, with plentiful supplies of German beer, had also raised worries.

But Dortmund police chief Bernhard Leidiger said the strategy of building a friendly atmosphere between rival supporters, which the city frequently employs for big European ties, had proved its value once again.
"English fans and Dortmund police did not have problems with each other," he said.
"The German fans' behaviour was also not substantially different from how they behave at normal league games. We're pleased the events at Porto didn't repeat themselves."
A senior British police officer who travelled to Dortmund to monitor the behaviour of the United fans agreed.
"The hand of friendship was extended and people responded," Superintendent Alan Hutchings of Greater Manchester Police said. "Overall, the behaviour of the English fans was very good indeed."
Hutchings said German police had been particularly impressed by the behaviour of the 3,500 United fans in Dortmund's Westfalen Stadium during the game.
But he said that although the street party in a city centre square had worked well, there will not be a similar event in Manchester at the return leg.
"It's not possible to do that back in England," he said.
The German police kept their presence at the party discreet while fans drank beer, sang and danced together in sunshine.
The mood was relaxed, with police donning the scarves of the two clubs, distributing souvenir stickers to fans and even taking photographs for them.
